## The Plan

1. Create a codespace on `main` of BusMgmtBenchmarks
2. Start Codex in the terminal with `codex.sh`
3. Sign in with a device code
4. Choose the `gpt-6-sol` model with `/model`
5. Ask Codex to make the **Export to Excel** button orange
6. Ask Codex to commit and push the change

## What You Need

- A GitHub account with access to [BusMgmtBenchmarks](https://github.com/calvinw/BusMgmtBenchmarks)
- A ChatGPT account to sign in to Codex
- The live app, to compare before and after: [Company vs Company](https://calvinw.github.io/BusMgmtBenchmarks/company_to_company.html)

## Why a Device Code?

- Codex runs on GitHub's computer, not on the computer in front of you
- It cannot open a browser window for you to sign in
- So it prints a link and a one-time code instead
- You sign in on your own browser tab and type in the code
- Only use a code that **your** Codex printed - never one someone gives you

## Check the Live Site

- The push starts the deploy in the repository's **Actions** tab
- Wait for the green check mark
- Reload [Company vs Company](https://calvinw.github.io/BusMgmtBenchmarks/company_to_company.html)
- The **Export to Excel** button is now orange

## Summary

- A codespace gives you VS Code and a terminal in the browser
- `codex.sh` starts the Codex agent in that terminal
- Sign in once with a device code, then pick a model with `/model`
- Describe the change in plain words and review what Codex edits
- Ask Codex to commit and push, and GitHub Pages publishes the new version
